picked.title: When the Simulator Fails, Not the Policy: Auditing Contact Artifacts in Simulated Robot Benchmarks
picked.summary: Simulation benchmarks score robot policies by success rate, and every failed episode counts against the policy. Many of these failures are the simulator's fault, not the policy's; we find the cause and fix it. Testing a vision language action model and a world action model in simulation, we find that the policy often places the object and the simulator then ejects it, and that the benchmark's own scripted demonstrations fail the same way. We present SimuGuard, an auditing plugin for LIBERO, RoboTwin, RoboCasa and RoboDojo. It leaves the evaluation unchanged. At every physics step, it records the state and flags an object that starts moving at a contact faster than the robot's contact or gravity account for. It replays a recorded episode bit for bit, and it reruns the episode with one simulation parameter changed. With it we trace these episodes on RoboTwin to the collision detection of the physics engine: for geometry one to two centimeters apart, the engine reports a penetration of about two centimeters, and the solver throws the object out at several meters per second. The cause is one constant: the distance algorithm discards triangles below a fixed area threshold, which valid triangles fall below at the centimeter scale. With that constant changed and nothing else, episodes with an artifact fall from 12 in 100 to none, and the success rate on five container tasks rises from 89% to 98%. Success rates in simulation thus count failures that the simulator causes. Benchmarks on PhysX 5.3.1 or earlier should rerun in a repaired engine. Where the engine cannot change, they should report the success rate together with the range it spans when every flagged episode fails or passes: 75.8% to 98.5% around a reported 83.1% for LingBot-VA.

picked.title: RTPolicy: Real-Time (32.9 Hz) Multi-View Visuomotor Policy for Robotic Manipulation on Edge Devices
picked.summary: Low inference latency is critical for closed-loop robotic manipulation, especially under asynchronous inference, where action chunks must be updated promptly to correct accumulated deviations. However, existing visuomotor policies rely on computationally expensive visual backbones, resulting in high inference latency and deployment overhead. In this paper, we propose RTPolicy, a multi-view visuomotor policy that attains accurate manipulation with high inference efficiency. Its core design combines view-aware feature fusion with visual compression to aggregate complementary information across camera views into a compact token representation. The representation conditions a flow-matching action generator with the robot state and flow time, reducing the cost of action generation. Extensive experiments demonstrate that this design reduces the computational cost of visual representation and action generation while preserving visual information required for manipulation. On the RoboTwin~2.0 single-task clean evaluation across 50 tasks, RTPolicy attains a mean success rate of 52.26\%, outperforming the strongest leaderboard baseline $π_0$ (46.4\%). We further evaluate RTPolicy under asynchronous streaming inference on a real bimanual platform, where RTPolicy attains a mean success rate of 72.0\% and sustains real-time inference at 30.35 ms (32.9 Hz) on the RDK S600 and 149.72 ms (6.7 Hz) on the RDK S100, both in INT16. Project Page: https://d-robotics-ai-lab.github.io/RTPolicy.project.

picked.title: Nexus-VLA: Bridging Human and Robot Experiences via a Shared Hierarchical Semantic Latent Space
picked.summary: Large-scale egocentric human videos provide rich and scalable manipulation experience for robot policy learning, yet substantial embodiment gaps in visual appearance, kinematic structure, and action spaces hinder effective knowledge transfer. Existing methods often decouple cross-embodiment knowledge alignment from robot policy learning, making it difficult for human manipulation knowledge to directly and fully contribute to robot action learning. To address this issue, we propose Nexus-VLA, a hybrid policy learning framework that enables cross-embodiment knowledge transfer through end-to-end human-robot joint training, allowing human manipulation experience to directly contribute to robot policy learning. We first introduce a hierarchical cross-embodiment semantic alignment paradigm that progressively establishes shared manipulation semantics from task intent to fine-grained interactions, enabling more complete use of the manipulation knowledge contained in human videos. Building on this hierarchy, we design a shared manipulation latent representation that jointly encodes multi-level shared knowledge into an internal representation directly used for continuous action generation, improving policy learning efficiency while effectively leveraging human knowledge. Across RoboCasa-GR1, OOD settings, and real-world robot experiments, Nexus-VLA achieves an 80.5% task success rate on RoboCasa-GR1 and demonstrates strong advantages in human-data utilization, learning efficiency, and cross-scenario generalization.

picked.title: Movens-Zero: Scaling Humanoid Motion Foundation Models with Large-Scale Human Videos
picked.summary: Scaling humanoid motion foundation models is constrained by the scarcity of diverse, robot-executable data and by the difficulty of jointly learning from heterogeneous multimodal inputs while supporting real-time closed-loop control. We present Movens-5M, constructed from raw Internet videos through clip generation, quality filtering, semantic annotation, motion recovery, and physical refinement with humanoid retargeting and execution verification. It contains 15 million human-motion sequences and 5 million physically executable humanoid-motion sequences spanning over 10,000 hours, aligned with text, RGB video, speech, and music. Building on this data, we introduce Movens-Zero, a scalable understanding-generation-execution architecture that supports joint learning across modalities and real-time closed-loop execution. Task-mixed flow-matching training jointly optimizes a single action expert across seven generation tasks, enabling direct motion generation from text, speech, music, and video. Multimodal Real-Time Chunking connects overlapping chunks under continuously updated instructions and robot states for continuous closed-loop execution. We further introduce Movens-Intent, a four-track benchmark with 8,192 expert-verified condition-motion pairs across text, speech, music, and video. Experiments show consistent gains across all four modalities when scaling execution-verified data from 1% to 100% and action-expert capacity from 64M to 911M parameters, while demonstrating that data quality and cross-modal supervision improve generation and execution.

picked.title: 破解智能体跨端协同办事难题，支付宝AHA方案获世界互联网大会“新耀”场景奖

picked.title: 阿里Qoder获世界互联网大会领先科技奖，已服务超800万用户、10万家企业
picked.summary: 11月2日，2026世界互联网大会颁奖典礼在浙江乌镇举行，全球共20项成果入选，涵盖量子计算、芯片、具身智能及AI应用等领域。凭借在智能体Harness上的技术突破和领先的全球市场份额，阿里智能体平台Qoder荣获领先科技奖，是国内唯一获得该奖项的通用Agent产品。 Qoder产品线总裁丁宇在现场领奖 世界互联网大会领先科技奖是面向科技和互联网领域的国际性科技奖项，旨在奖励全球年度最具领先性的互联网科技成果。今年，大会共征集来自43个国家和地区的430多项科技成果，经国内外权威专家严格评选，最终仅20项成果入选。 目前，AI编程是全球大模型应用落地最快的领域之一，也是全球顶尖模型创业公司和科技公司竞争的核心战场。依托于阿里巴巴多年在大模型、云计算与大规模工程实践上的积累，Qoder实现了模型、Agent运行框架与产品的联合设计，让智能体做到真正理解工程、自主编写工具、循环探索推进、完成研发任务，有效提升任务执行的效率。 Qoder还在不断拓展用户的使用场景。自2025年8月面向全球发布以来，Qoder产品家族已覆盖桌面版、AI 原生IDE、命令行工具CLI、JetBrains插件、数字员工产品QoderWake、云端Cloud Agents等产品，可满足不同用户习惯和应用场景的需求。用户不仅可以在电脑桌面端使用Qoder提效，也可以在手机上查看进度、审批操作、追加指令。企业级用户可以通过SDK ，把智能体嵌入到的产品中，从而快速实现智能化，还可以在云端运行长程任务，提供24小时不间断的主动工作、主动服务。 …

picked.title: 阿里云发布AI投研工作台Qovest，给专业投资者配一个“AI研究员”
picked.summary: 11月2日，阿里云正式发布面向专业机构投资者的AI投研工作台Qovest。用户用一句话提出研究需求，Qovest就会自动查数据、收集资料、深度分析、生成报告，并按设定的频率持续跟踪研究对象。与一次性问答不同，Qovest可以把每次的研究结果沉淀到投研空间，让一项研究能接着往下做，不必每次从零开始。近期，Qovest将推出企业版，服务金融机构及企业的投研团队。 专业投资者对Agent的要求，远比日常聊天要高：数据要实时和准确，输出结果要有明确出处，研究结论必须专业可靠。为此，Qovest团队采购权威金融数据库、将其部署在阿里云上，自研面向金融场景的Agent工程框架（Harness），打通从数据调用到分析输出的完整流程，让交付结果更加准确和专业。在开源金融评测集FinFirst与IRAB的内部横向评测中，Qovest的回答质量、响应速度、成本都领先于参与评测的主流产品。 “我们希望把投研过程中耗时较多、重复性较强的工作交给AI，把时间还给真正需要专业判断的地方。” Qovest产品负责人表示。 Qovest首页提供了多个投研案例范本，用户可以自选标的作为研究对象，设置定时任务，接入自己的操盘笔记，获得可视化的深度研究结果。比如，用户可以让Qovest拆解人形机器人产业链中各环节的单机价值与国产化水平，得到一份可交互的产业链图谱；也可以让Qovest测算数据中心电力设施的投资规模，只要调整任何一个前提假设，Qovest就会自动重新计算。 …

picked.title: 产业资本继续押注具身：斯坦福双子星创办的黑马公司 RoboScience 机器科学，宣布完成 A2 轮融资
picked.summary: 具身智能的资本筛选标准，正在从"讲得动人"转向"兑现得动"。AI 科技评论获悉，11 月 2 日，RoboScience 机器科学完成 A2 轮融资。 据悉，本轮由琥珀资本、鸿瑞达投资、上海半导体产投 联合领投，360 战投、爽资本、国联民生资本、金鼎资本及多家上市公司平台跟投，融资金额达到了数亿 元。 这意味着，这家 2025 年 3 月才正式开始运营的具身公司， 先后已完成五轮融资。 据 AI 科技评论了解，近期具身行业融资市场并不乐观。过去一年，这个赛道的融资叙事换了好几轮：最早讲世界模型就能拿到钱；后来光讲技术不够了，得讲落地，讲进工厂的 ROI ；再后来，得有"具身 RSI "（递归自我改进）的想象空间。 故事通胀的背后，是大多数团队的底子撑不起叙事的升级，每次风口转向，就得重新攒一套说辞。资本也随之变得挑剔，同样的 BP，去年能融到，今年连会都约不上。（雷峰网） 但 RoboScience 机器科学的节奏完全不同，逆势不断受到资本青睐，也因此成为具身领域里一个值得研究的样本公司。 回看机器科学过去五轮融资的时间点，几乎每一轮前后，都有可验证的产品技术落地：ICRA 最佳论文、仿真平台 RoboMirage、通用具身大模型 Visics、与腾讯云共创的云端具身智能服务 EaaS、首款轮式仿人形通用机器人 REX G1 以及真实的项目落地。 某种意义上，这意味着，具身市场的融资，不该是技术跟着融资的故事走，反过来，融资应该跟着技术的兑现走。 在 AI …
